title: Highlight the destination of a story link

# Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-270#highlight-linked-story-card

**Outcome: Assertion gap.**

- **Story and revision.** `.planning/seeds/SEED-270-highlight-linked-story-card.md#highlight-linked-story-card` at `520ce66952b58d529925868527962d14b43ff5bb` (plan `.planning/slice-plans/525-highlight-linked-story-card/PLAN.md`).
- **Promise.** "Following the same destination again shows the cue again, including when the card is already in view." Expected observable behavior: a repeat follow while a cue is still showing restarts the brief mark from its start, so the full brief cue plays again. I checked the reduced-motion static cue only through the baseline, because under reduced motion `animation: none` leaves no animation to restart. The plan records that removing the reduced-motion `animation: none` was already caught.
- **Fault.** `dashboard/src/destinationCue.ts`, `cueDestination`: I deleted the line `card.getBoundingClientRect();`, the forced layout between ending the showing cue and adding the class again. The class removal and re-add then fall in one style pass, so the existing CSS animation continues and does not restart. This fault differs from the ones the plan already recorded (removing the restart call, and cueing only the first reveal). Both of those were caught.
- **Fixture and maintained assertion.** `dashboard/tests/navigation/story-reference-navigation.spec.ts` › "a dependency opens its active story, keeping the dashboard and inspection on repeated activation". The test selects the supplier, follows the reference, passes 1000 ms of page time with `passPartOfCue`, and follows the reference again (the supplier card is already selected and in view). It then checks `expectDestinationCue(page, supplier, { motion: true })` (`dashboard/tests/destinationCue.ts`), passes 1000 ms more, checks `expectDestinationCue` again, and finally runs `expectCueEnds`. `expectDestinationCue` checks the cue class, that exactly one card is cued, that the `::after` content and box-shadow are not `none`, and the animation name. It does not check that the animation restarted or how far it has progressed.
- **Scratch checkout.** A detached `git worktree` at `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/6f54c3f6/tmp/ic-scratch` on the selected revision. Pre-probe state: 0 changes. Setup: `node scripts/setup-native.mjs npm` and `browser`, both exit 0. The execution checkout was not touched.
- **Command.** `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npm run test:dashboard -- <spec> -g "<title>" --workers=2 --reporter=list`, with logs `ic-baseline.log`, `ic-probe-baseline.log`, `ic-fault.log` and `ic-restored.log` under `/Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/6f54c3f6/tmp/`.
- **Independent behavior observation.** A temporary scratch spec, `dashboard/tests/navigation/zz-ic-probe.spec.ts`, followed the same fixture path. It tagged the cue's CSS animation (`card.getAnimations({subtree:true})`, `animationName === "story-card-destination-cue"`, `id = "first-cue"`), passed 1000 ms of page time, followed the reference again, and read the animation back.
  - The first probe attempt failed in fixture setup (`git commit` with nothing to commit, because I had omitted the `writePlanning` step). After I fixed that, the probe baseline passed: after the repeat, a new animation was running (`id ""`, `currentTime 0`, `startTime null`, meaning it was pending restart).
  - Under the fault: after the repeat, the original animation was still running (`id "first-cue"`, the same `startTime 877.87`, `currentTime 966.7 ms`). The 1600 ms cue holds full opacity until 40% (640 ms) and then fades with `forwards`. So the repeated cue was already fading and reaches opacity 0 about 630 ms later, while the class stays on for a further 1600 ms. The developer would see a fading or invisible mark instead of a fresh arrival cue. The wrong behavior is on the intended path: a repeat follow to an already-selected, in-view card while a cue is showing.
- **Run observations.**
  - Baseline: the maintained test passed (9.8 s) and exercised the selected test.
  - Fault: the maintained test still passed (11.2 s) with all assertions, including both post-repeat `expectDestinationCue` calls and `expectCueEnds`. In the same run, the probe failed with `expect(received).not.toBe(expected)`, expected not `"first-cue"`. So the intended assertion was reached and passed on the wrong behavior.
- **Restoration.** A shell `trap` ran `git checkout -- dashboard/src/destinationCue.ts` on exit, and I deleted the probe spec. `git diff --quiet HEAD` was clean, HEAD was still `520ce669`, and there were no untracked changes outside the ignored test results. The restored maintained test passed (8.8 s). I then removed the scratch worktree.
- **Note for strengthening (caller's decision).** In this run, the page-clock advance also advanced the cue animation's `currentTime` (about 967 ms after a 1000 ms `passPartOfCue`). That suggests a deterministic restart assertion is possible, for example comparing the animation's identity or `currentTime` before and after the repeat in `expectDestinationCue`. I did not verify how general this is.

## Cost

- **Test runtime.** Measured from Playwright's reported wall totals: baseline 13.6 s (maintained 9.8 s, with the probe's failed first attempt 5.3 s in the same run); probe baseline 9.0 s; fault run 12.4 s; restored run 9.8 s. Total about 44.8 s. Setup (`setup-native` npm and browser) is not included and was not timed separately.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no human took part in this check, and no separate measure exists.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: no separately supported measure of tokens or active agent time was available to this run. Wall time is covered by the elapsed entry below.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 147248 ms (measured), from 1794127224716 to 1794127371964 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.
